title: Singapore COE Category A quota premium, per bidding exercise
brief: Revision 3 (owner update 2026-11-10): production readiness now; no unscored trials. What will the Category A Certificate of Entitlement quota premium (S$, the clearing price paid by every successful bidder) be at the named LTA COE open bidding exercise, as first published in data.gov.sg dataset d_69b3380ad7e51aff3a7dcc84eba52b8a? All proposed future rounds are ordinary scored rounds. Existing measurement, baseline, capture and cancellation rules are unchanged.
question: What will the Category A Certificate of Entitlement quota premium (S$, the clearing price paid by every successful bidder) be at the named LTA COE open bidding exercise, as first published in data.gov.sg dataset d_69b3380ad7e51aff3a7dcc84eba52b8a?

target.population: Category A of Singapore's Vehicle Quota System as defined from the May 2022 1st exercise: non-fully-electric cars up to 1,600 cc and 97 kW, and fully electric cars up to 110 kW [verified, dataset description]. The premium is set by all individual and company bids in that category in that exercise.
target.window: One open bidding exercise, from its start (normally Monday 12:00 SGT) to its close (normally Wednesday 16:00 SGT), as dated in LTA's annual schedule. 2026 exceptions: February (2) runs Mon 16 Feb to Fri 20 Feb (Chinese New Year); June (1) runs Tue 2 Jun to Thu 4 Jun (Vesak Day in lieu) [verified, 2026 schedule].
target.calculation: The integer in field 'premium' of the row with month = the exercise month (YYYY-MM), bidding_no = '1' or '2', vehicle_class = 'Category A', read from the resolution capture. No arithmetic.

lock: One hour before the exercise's start time in LTA's schedule: normally Monday 11:00 SGT (03:00Z), changed from the doc's Monday 16:00 SGT. Reason: bidding opens at 12:00 SGT, and the doc itself says live bid counts are public on OneMotoring during bidding; LTA's COE page says the Current COE Price ('the price of the highest unsuccessful bid plus $1') rises during the exercise and 'The latest CCPs at the close of bidding are the Quota Premiums' [verified text, onemotoring COE page fetched 2026-11-09T01:00Z]. A lock after opening lets an entrant copy a running price. The live display during bidding was not observed (no exercise was open during this pass) [unverified]. The quota for the exercise is announced before it opens (LTA quarterly quota release, plus unallocated COEs carried over) [verified text, open-bidding page notes], so it is public at lock and the question text gives it. This is 53 hours before release instead of 48. Owner update 2026-11-10: no unscored trial requirement. Every admitted future round is scored, subject to the existing reference, capture and cancellation rules. First proposed scored lock: 2026-12-07T03:00:00Z. Publish on main before lock; a missing or invalid reference does not become a fabricated baseline.
baseline: Ranked zero point mean_k(k=1, lag=0, rms_n=26) (owner decision, rev 2; was named 'persistence_rms26' in rev 1): mean = the Category A premium of the previous exercise; sd = the root-mean-square of its own errors, i.e. the 26 most recent exercise-to-exercise changes, all read from the lock capture. Zero-point family (G1): one parameterised reference 'mean_k(k, lag, rms_n)': the mean of the k most recent eligible values in the lock capture, after skipping 'lag' newer ones not yet published, with sd = the root-mean-square of that same rule's errors over the rms_n most recent resolved targets in the lock capture (G2). Persistence is mean_k(k=1). The arena's default persistence spread (sd 1.5) must not be used: on a premium near S$130,000 it is a point forecast. Measured on the 48 exercises 2024-12 (2) to 2026-11 (1) (data.gov.sg capture 2026-11-09, which is also the first print, since revisions were not observed): previous-exercise reference MAE S$3,787 (3.45% of the S$109,856 mean of the last 52 exercises); mean of the last two exercises MAE S$4,171 (3.80%); last value plus last change MAE S$5,064 (4.61%); mean of the last four S$4,961 (4.52%). Persistence is the best of the four, so the series is close to a random walk and skill must come from knowing demand. Spread check (lesson 12), same 48 exercises: with the 26-exercise RMS spread the reference's mean CRPS is S$2,713, its 90% interval covers 94% of outcomes, and an entrant who submits the reference mean and only rescales its sd gains at most +0.1% (k 0.95); with a 13-exercise RMS spread: CRPS S$2,785, coverage 85%, best gain 0.0%; with the fixed sd 1.5: CRPS S$3,786, so submitting the reference with an honest spread would score +28% skill [verified computation]. Shown, not ranked: mean of the last two exercises. Shocks in the window: the three-week gaps (^ in the schedule) and quarter-start exercises (new quota) did not move Cat A more than others (mean |change| 3.87% at quarter starts vs 3.94% otherwise); for Cat B and E they did (5.73% vs 4.34%; 4.45% vs 2.89%). The largest recent moves: January 2026 (1) -6.8% then January (2) +7.3% (bids received rose from 1,658 to 2,303), and November 2026 (1) +5.3% (bids 1,574 to 2,018).
resolution: The first successful capture at or after the exercise's close + 2 hours (normally Wednesday 18:00 SGT) whose rows contain (month, bidding_no, 'Category A'). Observed publication: the November 2026 (1) exercise closed Wed 4 Nov 16:00 SGT and the dataset's lastUpdatedAt was 2026-11-04T17:37:51+08:00 (98 minutes); the doc reports 73 minutes for October (1) [verified for November; October is owner input]. The arena refresh runs every 6 hours, so the round is resolved by the first refresh after close + 2 h, within at most 6 hours more. The archived bodies (bytes, sha256, request URL, fetched_at) are the record; a later change to the row never changes a resolved round. OneMotoring shows the same results at close [verified: the open-bidding page listed 2026-11 (1) Cat A quota 1,189, premium 139,001, matching data.gov.sg], but it is not the resolution source.
missing_data_policy: (1) No capture containing the row by close + 48 hours (normally Friday 16:00 SGT): the round is cancelled, never resolved from a later pull. (2) If LTA moves an exercise after the round is posted, and the new start is still after the lock, the round follows the new dates and the lock moves with it, announced before the old lock; if the new start would be before the posted lock, the round is cancelled. If the exercise is cancelled, so is the round. (3) If LTA changes the Category A definition between posting and close (LTA is consulting on a new car categorisation, per the doc), the round is cancelled. (4) A premium of 0 or a missing premium with quota > 0 (no rows like this were seen since 2010; not checked for every row) is treated as missing under (1). (5) The reference at lock needs 27 consecutive exercises in the lock capture; if any is missing, the round is not posted.
scoring: SSA topline scoring: mean and sd (sd > 0) or a quantile map including 0.5, scored with CRPS; arena target_type continuous_normal. Skill = 1 - CRPS(entrant) / CRPS(zero point mean_k(k=1, rms_n=26)). Noise check (arena scoring.noise_floor, last 52 exercises since May 2022): Category A premium m = 0, s = S$4,698 per exercise; the premium is a clearing price with no sampling noise, so the arena score's ceiling term is 0 and the persistence error is the gate (docs/sources.md §1.4), which it passes (mean |change| 3.46%). Also shown, not ranked: skill against the mean of the last two exercises, median absolute error, and 50%/90% interval coverage. Two rounds a month at most, so a season produces about 24 scored rounds a year.

[verified computation, capture 2026-11-09, 52 exercises since May 2022 for movement, 48 targets for errors] Premium, persistence MAE by category: A S$3,787 (3.45%), B 4,444 (3.68%), C 1,639 (2.14%), D 454 (4.83%), E 3,091 (2.53%). Mean of last two is worse in every category (A 3.80%). arena noise_floor: A m 0 s 4,698; B m 1,232 s 5,467; C m 0 s 2,024; D m 0 s 538; E m 0 s 4,419. Cat D does not fail the noise check, contrary to the doc's warning; its persistence error is the largest in relative terms. Bids received, persistence MAE: A 201 (11.0%), B 130 (11.1%), C 33 (7.8%), D 34 (5.4%), E 44 (10.1%); for B to E the mean of the last four beats persistence (B 9.0%). Correlation of quota change with premium change: A -0.22, B -0.27, E 0.01.

[verified computation, rev 1 spread check, 48 Cat A targets 2024-12 (2) to 2026-11 (1)] Reference = previous premium. sd = RMS of last 26 changes: mean CRPS 2,713, best rescale gain +0.1% (k 0.95), 90% coverage 0.94, sd S$3,797-6,767. sd = RMS of last 13: 2,785, 0.0%, 0.85, sd 2,537-6,558. Fixed sd 1.5: 3,786 (+28% free skill). Same check for B (26: +0.9%, cov 0.92) and E (26: +2.9%, cov 0.94).

assumptions: Owner update 2026-11-10: remove the unscored trial requirement and prepare production immediately. Data validity and baseline gates remain mandatory.

Dataset and question chosen within the group without asking: COE is the strongest of the five Singapore sources on SSA's gates (written licence, automated API use named in writing, a publisher schedule, keyless). Runner-up: taxi availability (keyless, spatial), but SSA would define and resolve its metric.
Lock set to one hour before the scheduled start, not at the start, so that a refresh that runs late or a clock difference cannot push the lock into the exercise. Runner-up: exactly 12:00 SGT.

Resolution at close + 2 h on data.gov.sg, not OneMotoring at close. Reason: data.gov.sg is the licensed, machine-readable copy; OneMotoring is an LTA web page without a dataset licence. Runner-up: archive OneMotoring as a cross-check only.
Grace window 48 hours (to Friday 16:00 SGT). Reason: publication took 98 minutes; 48 h covers a weekend-free delay without letting a much later file resolve a round. Easy to change.

Suggested arena names, for implementation: tracker 'sg_coe'; series 'sg_coe_premium_cat_a'; adapter ssa/adapters/sg_coe.py with a fetch_text/parse split; archive sources/coe/; round_id 'sg-coe-a-<YYYY-MM>-<n>'. Naming only.
